newsitem.title: INDIA: Lehman Bros says right time to enter Indian market.
newsitem.headline: Lehman Bros says right time to enter Indian market.

text.p: Securities firm Lehman Brothers said it thought the time was right to invest in Indian markets.
"We are overweight on the Indian market from a 12-month perspective," Lehman said in its latest India review.
"In anticipation, we believe this is a good time to enter the market," it said.

Lehman said it was not enthusiastic about the rally at the beginning of 1996 since it was dominated by foreign flows without any domestic support. The rally was also unsupported by any meaningful improvement in surplus liquidity, it said.

"The situation currently is that liquidity is ample and relative yields are moving in favour of equities from a domestic investor perspective and with a forecast decline in interest rates and a pick up in the economy later this year," it said.
Lehman said the surplus liquidity put the market in a pre-bull phase. "The current poor sentiment represents an opportunity to buy," it said.
"Our 12-month target for the Sensex (Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index) is 4,750, representing an upside of 33 percent in rupee terms and 21 percent in dollar terms," it said.

It said easier liquidity conditions have resulted in significant declines in yields on government and corporate bonds. In the longer term, multiple expansion for the markets will be driven by growth considerations rather than short-term liquidity factors, Lehman said.

"Multiple expansion will largely be driven by the economy's ability to gravitate toward growth rates closer to 7.0-8.0 percent in line with regional neighbours such as Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia and away from the 5.0 percent real growth achieved over the past 10 years," the report said.

It said the policy framework required for achieving more ambitious growth targets appeared to be in place. "The risk lies in possible slippage in execution given the somewhat tentative political situation."

If a transition to a higher growth rate is achieved, the Indian market appears to offer value on a price/earning to growth basis at a time when several of its regional neighbours are experiencing sharply decelerating growth, it said.
Lehman listed the following factors which could depress near-term sentiment -- politics, the July budget and the earnings outlook.

"While we continue to believe that the cyclical nature of Indian earnings implies that FY 1996/97 (April-March) earnings are vulnerable to disapppointments, the outlook for FY98 appears improved given the favourable growth and interest rate outlook," it added.
